channels.eog_note: Second EOG channel is HEOR in the EDF but VEOR (vertical) in the BIDS sidecar: UNVERIFIED. Each EOG channel is used separately; no bipolar HEOL-HEOR derivation.
channels.analysed_channels_note: The 22 channels of the 11 extended homologous pairs (v2 G24f pairs renamed to 10-10). Fp1/Fp2 and midline excluded.

filter.notch_note: No notch: 50 Hz lies beyond the 40 Hz FIR stop band. 50 Hz residue is measured and reported (relative 48-52 Hz power before and after filtering).

bad_channels.method: pyprep.NoisyChannels (PREP; Bigdely-Shamlo et al. 2015) on the continuous, unfiltered recording (pyprep detrends at 1 Hz internally); reference channel CPz and EOG channels excluded from detection
bad_channels.max_bad_channels_rule: Reviewer rule (Step 2 review): a subject with more than 9 bad channels (> 31% of the 29 detectable channels) is flagged and ICA is NOT run, so ICA never runs with fewer than the configured 20 components (rank = 29 - n_bad). In final mode the subject is excluded with reason 'too_many_bad_channels'. Correction to the Step 2 status PDF: EOG z-score detection itself remains possible down to 11 components (max attainable z (n-1)/sqrt(n) > 3 needs n >= 11), i.e. it would only become impossible above 18 bad channels; the 9-channel guard is stricter by design.
bad_channels.note: All detection thresholds are the PREP published defaults; none was tuned on this cohort.

reference.rule: 1) Average reference over good EEG channels with CPz included as the zero-valued online reference. 2) Spherical-spline interpolation of bad channels from the re-referenced good channels, except channels whose homologous partner is also bad (pair unavailable; channels stay marked bad, not interpolated). 3) Average reference again over all available channels.

ica.n_components_rule: min(20, data rank) with rank = 29 - n_bad_channels; equals 20 whenever the bad-channel guard passes
ica.remove: union of components flagged by any EOG channel

epochs.source: marker_onset of usable trials in results/v3/step1/marker_events.csv (never the shared sidecar)

screen_rules.all_scalp: 150 uV peak-to-peak on every available scalp EEG channel (CPz included after re-referencing; unavailable-pair channels excluded).
screen_rules.analysed: 150 uV peak-to-peak on the 22 analysed channels only (Fp1/Fp2 and midline not screened).
screen_rules.analysed_after_marking: Before screening, any analysed channel that alone exceeds 150 uV in >= 30% of the subject's epochs is marked bad and interpolated on the epochs (left bad, pair unavailable, if its homologous partner is also bad), the average reference is re-applied, then rule 'analysed' is applied.

epochs.final_screen_rule_note: Chosen by the user from the label-free diagnostic run (--mode diagnostic). Final mode refuses to run until this is one of the screen_rules keys.

class_balance.rule: Replaces left/right count equalization (handoff Step 2.8; reviewer change). All clean epochs are kept; each kept epoch's class (left_hand/right_hand) is saved in the epoch events and metadata. Later feature steps compute every feature per class and average the two class means, so each class has equal weight without discarding epochs.

min_epochs.proposed_rule: >= 10 clean epochs in each class (left and right) under the chosen screen rule
min_epochs.rule: Fixed only from the label-free epoch-count distribution of the diagnostic run; reported to the user before it is applied.

heog_check.statistic: Per subject, Spearman rho across epochs between AI = (L-R)/(L+R) band power and log EOG band power; before ICA (re-referenced, interpolated) vs after ICA, same epochs. Diagnostic mode: all usable (unscreened) epochs. Final mode: kept epochs.
